slides.0.title: The Breede River Valley and the interior
slides.0.subtitle: Robertson, Worcester, Breedekloof, Klein Karoo, Olifants River
slides.1.title: The Breede River Valley
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Area in 2025
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Robertson about 13,067 ha, Breedekloof about 12,679 ha, Worcester about 6,404 ha (Worcester is described as the most important brandy-producing area)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Robertson's lime-rich soils
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Known for lime-rich soils (calcium carbonate), with Bonnievale and Klaasvoogds notably high in lime; Chardonnay is the dominant variety
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Reliance on irrigation
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Rainfall is about 250–400 mm a year, the Breede River crosses the District and supplies irrigation, and day-night swings of 15–20°C preserve acidity
slides.1.content: The Breede River Valley is a high-volume inland valley irrigated from the river, and its lime-rich soils make Robertson Chardonnay famous.
slides.2.title: Klein Karoo
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Structure
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The Region has two Districts (Calitzdorp and Langeberg-Garcia) and five stand-alone Wards (Montagu, Outeniqua, Tradouw, Tradouw Highlands, Upper Langkloof)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Cape Port styles
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Calitzdorp is the centre of Cape Port-style wines using Portuguese varieties such as Touriga Nacional; since 2012 EU–South Africa rules require "Cape" prefixes such as Cape Vintage and Cape Tawny instead of "Port"
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Aridity
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Calitzdorp gets about 200 mm of rain a year and vineyards are almost all irrigated
slides.2.content: Klein Karoo is dry and hot; Cape Port styles are its speciality.
slides.3.title: The Olifants River
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Position and makeup
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The northernmost of the Western Cape's five Regions; Districts are Citrusdal Mountain, Citrusdal Valley and Lutzville Valley, and Spruitdrift, Vredendal and Bamboes Bay are stand-alone Wards
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Cooperatives
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Four major cooperative cellars (Vredendal, Namaqua, Klawer, Lutzville) process most of the volume and supply bulk wine; area was about 8,238 ha in 2025
slides.3.highlights.2.title: High-altitude Cederberg
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The Cederberg ward sits at about 1,030 m and is described as South Africa's highest commercial vineyard zone
slides.3.content: Orange River and other Northern Cape areas are outside this lesson's verified scope and would need official sources before being added.
